title: Lesson 1: f-strings
lessonSummary: Great! With f-strings you build stable messages without worrying about str() and +.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and watch how the variables travel into the text.
tasks.codeTemplate:
rider = "Sarah"
horse = "Luna"
discipline = "Dressage"
print(f"{rider} and {horse} are training {discipline}!")

validation.expected: Sarah and Luna are training Dressage!

tasks.instruction: Use an f-string to print exactly this sentence: Hello Thunder! You are 8 years old!

validation.expected: Hello Thunder! You are 8 years old!

tasks.instruction: Calculate the sum inside the f-string's braces and print exactly: Daily feed: 5 kg

title: Lesson 2: Walk – Text (str)
lessonSummary: Step by step: everything in quotation marks is text – and type() reveals it.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. type() is a function – it names the type for you.
Use type() to print the type of the variable breed.
What type does the variable hoof_number have? Print it with type().

title: Lesson 3: Trot – Whole Numbers (int)
lessonSummary: The trot moves forward countably: whole numbers are called int.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at the type.
tasks.codeTemplate:
age = 7
height = 168  # cm
print(f"Age: {age} years, height: {height} cm")
print(type(age))

tasks.instruction: Create age = 9 and use an f-string to print exactly: Age: 9 years
A horse is 168 cm tall, a pony 138 cm. Store the difference in the variable difference and print exactly: Difference: 30 cm

title: Lesson 4: Canter – Decimal Numbers (float)
lessonSummary: Flowing like a canter: decimal numbers are called float and use a point.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at the type.
tasks.codeTemplate:
weight = 550.5
feed_amount = 4.25
print(f"Weight: {weight} kg, feed: {feed_amount} kg")
print(type(weight))

tasks.instruction: A horse eats 4.25 kg of feed per day. Print for 2 days exactly: Feed for 2 days: 8.5 kg
Create the variable height_m with the value 1.68 and print its type with type().

title: Lesson 5: Jump – Truth Values (bool)
lessonSummary: A jump succeeds or it fails: truth values only know True and False.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at the type.
tasks.codeTemplate:
has_saddle = True
is_visited = False
print(f"Has saddle: {has_saddle}")
print(f"Is visited: {is_visited}")
print(type(has_saddle))

tasks.instruction: Create is_healthy = True and use an f-string to print exactly: Healthy: True
Compare the age with 10 and print the result of the comparison `age > 10` with print().

title: Lesson 6: Calculating with Numbers
lessonSummary: You calculate like a pro – and now know that / always gives a decimal number.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at the results.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horses_a = 12
horses_b = 8
print(f"Total horses: {horses_a + horses_b}")
print(f"Difference: {horses_a - horses_b}")
print(f"Double stables: {horses_a * 2}")
print(f"Horses per box: {horses_a / 4}")

tasks.instruction: 12 horses stand in 4 boxes. Print exactly: Horses per box: 3.0
Each of the 12 horses gets 3 kg of hay. Calculate the total weight and print exactly: Hay total: 36 kg

title: Lesson 7: Calculating with Text
lessonSummary: Texts have operators too – you can add and multiply them, but never mix them with numbers!

tasks.instruction: Run this example.
tasks.codeTemplate:
name = "Star"
suffix = "light"
full_name = name + suffix
print(f"Full name: {full_name}")
print(f"Neigh: {name * 3}")

tasks.instruction: Join the two texts into full_name and print exactly: Full name: Morningstar
Make the horse neigh three times: use * to print exactly: Neigh! Neigh! Neigh!

title: Lesson 8: Converting Types
lessonSummary: Converting with int(), float(), str() and bool() – four functions for four types.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and compare the types before and after converting.
tasks.codeTemplate:
age_text = "5"
age_number = int(age_text)
print(f"Age as text: {age_text} (type: {type(age_text)})")
print(f"Age as number: {age_number} (type: {type(age_number)})")
print(float("4.5"))
print(str(5))
print(bool(1))

tasks.instruction: Convert the text kg_text with int() and print exactly: 15 kg of hay will last 30 days.

validation.expected: 15 kg of hay will last 30 days.

tasks.instruction: Convert the text portion_text with float(), double the portion and print exactly: Double portion: 9.0 kg

title: Lesson 9: Processing Input
lessonSummary: Input is always text – with int() you make it usable for calculations.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and type a whole number into the input box, e.g. 15.
tasks.codeTemplate:
answer = input("How many kg of hay? ")
number = int(answer)
print(f"{number} kg of hay will last {number * 2} days.")

tasks.instruction: Ask with input() for your horse's age, convert the answer with int() and print: Next year: (age plus 1) (When checking, 8 is entered automatically.)
